findings.description: The method extracts 'code' and 'libraries_used' from kwargs without validating presence, null values, or data types.
findings.impact: Passing invalid or unvalidated inputs can lead to type errors, unexpected fallback execution, or script injection.
findings.remediation: Validate that required kwargs exist and are of expected types before passing them to execution routines.

findings.description: Execution output is returned directly from the interpreter functions without sanitization, filtering, or size limits.
findings.impact: Raw execution outputs containing indirect prompt injections or excessively large text can compromise model context or control flow.
findings.remediation: Sanitize and truncate execution output before returning it to the LLM agent.

findings.description: The tool executes arbitrary user-supplied code directly on the host in unsafe_mode without human confirmation or approval gates.
findings.impact: An LLM agent can execute destructive or unauthorized system commands autonomously without user oversight.
findings.remediation: Require explicit user confirmation before executing code in unsafe mode.

findings.description: Exposing 'run_code_unsafe' alongside sandboxed execution tools enables execution environment bypass and host system compromise.
findings.evidence: While 'run_code_in_docker' and 'run_code_in_restricted_sandbox' provide isolated environments, tool 'run_code_unsafe' allows an agent—or an adversary via prompt injection—to bypass sandboxing entirely and execute unconstrained Python code directly on the host machine.
findings.impact: Full execution privileges on the host system, potentially resulting in host-level data exfiltration, persistence, or complete host takeover.
findings.remediation: Deprecate and remove 'run_code_unsafe' from the set of tools accessible to the agent. Enforce containerized execution via mandatory platform policy rather than agent decision-making.
